title: Playing the Dew Drop and nightly pay
summary: Two years at the Dew Drop around 1954-56 for about $15 a night, and union scale.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Yeah. See, at the Dew Drop, that's another thing. See, I played at the Dew Drop at one stretch, and I'll say I've been trying to remember, it had to be before I went to Milano, and I think around 1954. I played there almost two years straight. And I think so, because when I left the Dew Drop, I went to, I went up on Oak Street. So it was either 55, all of, I think all of 55 I was in the Dew Drop. And part of 56, you know, maybe the end of 54, all of 55, part of 56, I was playing Dew Drop every night. Friday, Saturday, Sunday. Making about $15.
About a night? Uh-huh. Was that kind of standard?
Kind of, yeah, kind of standard. $15, well, $10 was the standard thing. See, at one time it was eight. I think it went up to ten, and I think I probably made fifteen.
Now, was that union scale, or was that what Dwight paid? No, that was union scale.
Eight dollars was union scale. And what, what assignment did you get it? Well, no, no, well, I made, well, if I made fifteen, the assignment must have got eight. Oh, okay. Or maybe ten.
